$description: Kiwi UI design tokens — Ruled Folio. One DTCG source (W3C Design Tokens format, stable Oct 2025) in three tiers: global (the locked block of kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md), semantic (roles; palette.mjs aliases carried by reference + Phase 3 additions), component (one group per shared component, eight states each). Modes: $value is light / comfortable; $extensions.mode.dark and .compact carry the overrides (two orthogonal axes). Spec: kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Design system. Check: .design-foundations/tokens/check-tokens.mjs. Emit: build-tokens.mjs.

org.kiwi.deprecationPolicy: A deprecated name keeps a safe value and is removed no earlier than two MAJOR versions after the release that deprecated it, and no earlier than six months after that release, whichever is later; the checker asserts the removal major.

.kiwi-bg-secondary.note: one accent hue; the pink secondary is retired

.kiwi-spinner.note: progress is neutral text with the text dots, never a spinner

@keyframes kiwi-spin.note: no spinning glyph in the motion budget

.kiwi-step-connector.note: restyled: a neutral hairline; [data-done] marks the span up to the current step

.kiwi-step-pending.note: a pending step is the indicator's default: hairline boundary, secondary text

.kiwi-step-active.note: the current step is state by attribute, not by class; selection tint, no glow

.kiwi-step-completed.note: a completed step: the success surface with the check glyph (status = surface + icon)

.kiwi-step-error.note: a failed step: the error surface with the cross glyph

.kiwi-step-connector-active.note: the connector has one neutral emphasis, not a brand fill

.kiwi-progress-dots.note: progress is neutral text with the text dots (G9); stages that finished or failed are status chips (.kiwi-chip-status-*)

.kiwi-progress-dot-active.note: no pulsing dot: the text dots carry the motion

.kiwi-progress-dot-completed.note: a finished stage is a success status chip

.kiwi-progress-dot-error.note: a failed stage is an error status chip

.kiwi-progress-bar.note: restyled: the neutral determinate bar, --kiwi-border-interactive on --kiwi-bg-hover

.kiwi-progress-bar-indeterminate.note: an indeterminate sweep is outside the motion budget; a determinate .kiwi-progress-bar stays

@keyframes kiwi-pulse.note: no pulsing in the motion budget

@keyframes kiwi-progress-indeterminate.note: no sweeping gradient in the motion budget

.kiwi-help.note: the reason or helper line under a control, linked by aria-describedby; data-state="error" or "success" takes the status text colour

org.kiwi.literalPolicy: Colour literals: hex only in global.*; semantic.color.logo.* (G2) and semantic.color.on-paper.* (G5, mode-frozen) are the only colour literals outside it; backdrop and shadow.* reference --shadow-ink and carry their alphas in $extensions["org.kiwi"].alpha, composed by the emitter. Component tier: every value is a reference to the semantic tier except a literal marked $extensions["org.kiwi"].literal with its reason (component-specific geometry: the checker lists the marked ones and fails on any other). Forms the guard catches outside the source: hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla(), hwb(), oklch()/oklab(), lab()/lch(), color(), color-mix(), light-dark(), named colours other than transparent, currentColor and inherit, palette-object imports, and the MUI palette paths that bypass the roles: the strings "grey.NN" and "common.white" / "common.black", and the accesses theme.palette.grey[...] / palette.grey.NN and palette.common.* (common allowed in src/components/Brand/InstitutionLogo.tsx only, G2); the scan covers src/** outside src/services/, index.html, public/*.webmanifest, public/**/*.svg (the mascot artwork allowlisted) and .storybook/**.

reserved.chart.*: Phase 6 registered chart.series.1-5, chart.other and the chart chrome roles here (2026-10-18), replacing the interim palette.chart stand-ins; the MUI theme's palette.chart now reads them.
reserved.companion.*: Phase 4 registered companion.slot.* and companion.backing here (2026-10-17); chart.* stays reserved for Phase 6.

standard.$description: menus, popovers, the chat panel, dialogs, toasts entering

shimmer.$description: the skeleton sweep, the one permitted moving gradient

semantic.$description: Tier 2. Roles. Colour aliases (carried + additions), editor/syntax/console roles, shadows, density deltas (space, size, type), motion, layers.

color.$description: The semantic aliases of the locked block, carried as references so they stay identical by construction (per-mode overrides as locked; re-pointed by the 2026-10-18 re-lock), then the additions registered by Phase 3. CSS names of the carried aliases are the locked names.

background.$description: Canvas (page). Locked override: the cream canvas (the reference's page) / the forest-black dark canvas.

surface.$description: Sheet (panels, dialogs, inputs, the chat panel): always the lighter step.

surface-hover.$description: Hover rows and controls; tonal, instant.

surface-active.$description: Pressed rows, role chips, disabled fills, the in-progress surface.

text-secondary.$description: Secondary text, chrome icons at rest, disabled labels.

accent-bg-subtle.$description: The hover tint of secondary and tertiary controls and rows that tint (the reference's button hover).

accent-bg-subtle-active.$description: The pressed tint of secondary and tertiary controls (the reference's sage stage): two steps past the accent-3 hover tint, past the accent-4 selected fill (the functional ramps have no fourth step, so the outlined destructive keeps error-3 and the scale on press).

accent-solid.$description: The one filled control per region, Soft sage (the user's pick, 2026-10-18): a sage tint deeper than the selected fill, with the forest label and a 1 px --accent-solid-border edge. The fill is a tint, not the control's boundary (about 1.4:1 on the sheet): the edge is.

accent-solid-hover.$description: Hover of the filled control: one step deeper.

accent-solid-active.$description: The pressed fill of a filled control: one step beyond hover, so pressed is told from hovered by its fill and not by the 0.98 scale alone (light accent-8 past the accent-7 hover; dark accent-8 past the accent-7 hover), with --accent-on-solid at 4.5:1 or more on it.

accent-solid-border.$description: The 1 px edge of the filled control, Send and the launcher: their boundary (≥ 3:1 on the canvas and the sheet in both modes), since the Soft sage fill is a tint. Light: the reference's strong green (also the focus ring); dark: the derived sage edge.

accent-on-solid.$description: The label on the filled control: the forest in light, the dark ink in dark.

accent-text.$description: Links (underlined), accent text and icons, secondary/tertiary button labels.

border-interactive.$description: The ≥3:1 boundary of every control identified by a border: inputs, unchecked controls, unselected filter chips, grips. neutral-10, the derived field edge (the reference's hairline is 1.25:1, a divider only).

focus-ring.$description: One frame (the user's decision of 2026-10-19): a control with a border shows focus by recolouring that border to --focus-ring at 2 px, the extra pixel inward, so nothing shifts; a control with no border shows one 2 px ring, its only frame (2 px offset, or inset 2 px inside clipped rails, tab bars, rows and menus). Hover, selected, pressed and error recolour the frame too, never stack a second one. :focus-visible; never removed, never animated; forced colours: Highlight. accent-10: the reference's strong green in light, its toggle accent in dark.

shadow-ink.$description: The hue-shifted shadow colour (light: the reference's forest; dark: the lock's green-black); shadows are precomputed rgba() of it.

link.$description: Links in prose and chrome; always underlined in prose (WCAG 1.4.1).

selection.$description: The lock's selection rule: the selected fill + accent text + a 2 px solid marker. Since the 2026-10-18 re-lock the selected fill is its own step (accent-4, the reference's pressed-button fill), one step past the hover tint, and the marker is the strong green (accent-10). Also the on/checked state of switches, checkboxes and radios. Under forced-colors: active a box-shadow computes to none, so every marker selector also draws the marker as a 2 px Highlight outline (outline-offset −2 px) inside @media (forced-colors: active), and the dots, dash and thumb that are backgrounds take CanvasText there; glyph, weight and position cues survive as system colours.

destructive.$description: Destructive controls are outlined, never filled (D4): error-11 boundary and label, error-3 hover tint.

status.$description: Status surfaces (G1): -3 surface, -11 text and shape icon, -9 only as a dot or small fill beside a label.

in-progress.$description: In progress is neutral (G1, TD-29): surface-active + text-secondary + the static dashed-ring icon; the moving part is the text dots.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls: fill, label and hairline. Exempt from WCAG 1.4.3/1.4.11; the shared trio keeps a read label at ≥ 4.5 (fields, checkboxes, tabs, menus). Buttons fade further, by the user's decision of 2026-10-18 ("淡化即可（推荐）"; plan Decision Log, "Disabled buttons"): a disabled button may be faint, and keeps every enabled requirement in its enabled states; it is told from its enabled self by a lower-luminance label and edge, the disabled primary keeps a faint sage fill (disabled.solid) so it is never the disabled secondary, and no disabled button looks like a hovered tertiary (it has an edge and a fainter label). Every disabled control states why (helper text or a toggletip on the aria-disabled control itself); under forced colours its border and text are GrayText.

icon.$description: Disabled icon-only controls (no fill to distinguish them).

solid.$description: The disabled primary's faint sage fill: one step fainter than the Soft sage fill (light accent-5, dark accent-4), so a disabled primary is still the primary and never the disabled secondary's sheet, and not a hovered tertiary's tint (accent-3).

solid-border.$description: The disabled primary's faint sage edge: still an edge, lower than the enabled --accent-solid-border (light accent-9, the mascot's sage; dark accent-8). Not gated: WCAG 1.4.11 exempts inactive controls.

outline.$description: The disabled outlined button's faint edge (secondary, destructive): the ruler's step, lower than the enabled --border-interactive. Not gated.

label.$description: A disabled button's label: lower in luminance than the enabled label in both modes. In light it is secondary text; in dark secondary text sits at accent text's luminance, so the label drops to neutral-10. Not gated: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive controls.

skeleton.$description: Loading placeholders; the shimmer highlight is the one permitted moving gradient.

icon.$description: Icons are currentColor; these are the resting colours in chrome.

paper-frame.$description: The neutral frame around paper (PDF pages, email previews, app iframes): never the accent (G5, TD-08).

fill-none.$description: The transparent fill of text-only and canvas-level components (tertiary buttons, icon buttons, tabs, rows, the empty frame, the tutor row): a role, so the component tier carries no literal.

backdrop.$description: Dialog and modal backdrops: --shadow-ink at 40 % (light) / 60 % (dark). The colour is a reference; the alphas live in $extensions["org.kiwi"].alpha and the emitter composes the rgba() per mode, so a change of ink cannot drift it. Never a grey wash, no blur. Declared per mode because it depends on a mode token.

logo.$description: Institution logos are neutral black or white by surface, never the accent, never the tinted ink (G2). The one permitted pure black / pure white.

on-light.$description: On light surfaces, in either mode.

on-dark.$description: On dark surfaces, in either mode.

on-paper.$description: Marks drawn on the white PDF page. The page keeps its own rendering in dark mode (G5), so these never follow the mode: light-ramp values frozen as literals, the allowlisted exception beside backdrop, shadows and the G2 logo. The pin, chunk and wash literals name their light source in $extensions["org.kiwi"].frozen and check-tokens.mjs asserts they still equal it, so a change of the ramps cannot leave them behind.

checkbox.$description: Checkboxes and radios: selection controls (D4), one family with one colour rule. An 18 px box (a radio: the same box with --radius-round and an 8 px dot) at --checkbox-size with the --border-interactive boundary on --surface; checked and indeterminate = the selection tint fill with the --selection-text glyph (the check, the dash, the dot), so the state is a shape change, never the hue alone; the label (--type-label at weight 400) is the accessible name and is clickable; a group has a group label and one helper line. disabled.$description: Disabled: the disabled trio (--disabled-surface fill, --disabled-border boundary, a --disabled-icon glyph if checked) and the label in --disabled-text at weight 400, with the reason stated in the group's helper or the row's reason and linked by aria-describedby; the box stays focusable (aria-disabled); a row that cannot be acted on disables its checkbox this way ("Professors are removed by an admin").

hit.$description: The hit area of a tab: 44 px on coarse pointers

Title --type-section-title, body at the page's density, body measure ≤ 75ch. Actions right-aligned: one filled primary, the Soft sage button with its edge (or the outlined destructive for confirmations), and a tertiary Cancel. Focus moves to the first focusable element, the background is inert, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger. Enter: fade + 8 px translate, 220 ms; exit 176 ms. Keyboard: on open focus moves to the first focusable element (the title for confirmations), Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger; the background is inert.

width-md.$description: The dialog's maximum width; the drawn width is min(100% - 2 * var(--space-popup-margin), var(--dialog-width-md)), so on a phone the sheet keeps a 12 px margin and never exceeds the viewport

The same pattern draws the toast's and the banner's actions, so a text action looks one way everywhere and its affordance does not depend on hover. The neutral variant is the in-progress notice (ring icon + dots). action-underline-hover.$description: the text action's underline on hover and while pressed

toast.$description: Toasts (snackbars): a --surface sheet with --shadow-1 and a 1 px --border, width: min(100% - 2 × --toast-edge-offset, --toast-max-width) (at most 420 px; on a 390 px phone 342 px, the launcher's 24 px kept from both edges), entering from the bottom edge by 8 px in 220 ms. Neutral text, or a status icon + label in the status's -11. Bottom-right 24/16 px measured from the safe area (bottom: calc(var(--toast-offset-y) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); bottom-left on app tabs, beside the launcher); one at a time. Timing (WCAG 2.2.1): an info or success toast without an action auto-dismisses after 6 s, and its timer pauses while the pointer is over it, while anything inside it has focus (focus-within) and while the window has lost focus; a toast that carries an action (Undo after a removal) stays until dismissed, or at least 10 s under the same pause rules; error toasts persist until dismissed. Every toast carries Dismiss; an error toast adds Retry where a retry exists; an Undo toast shows Undo beside Dismiss. Keyboard path: the toast is rendered immediately after the control that raised it, so it is the next tab stop (one Tab from the trigger reaches Undo or Dismiss, Shift+Tab returns); the live region announces the message, and an error toast (role=alert) takes focus while an info or success toast (role=status) does not; Escape dismisses the focused toast. Queue: a new info or success toast replaces a visible info or success toast that carries no action; a toast with an action and an error toast are never replaced silently: they stay until dismissed and later toasts queue behind them (first in, first out, at most three queued; identical messages collapse into one with a count).

radius.$description: A toast is a floating sheet: --radius-sheet (8 px)

icon-size.$description: The status icon (24 comfortable / 20 compact), like the alert's

tutor-message.$description: The tutor-message surface: a tutor row is a 32 px avatar slot (G9) + 12 px gap + the answer column, on the message region's ruler (text 68 px right of the rule). Answer text --type-body 16/24, CJK-dominant blocks 28, measure 68ch, blocks 12 px apart, messages 24 px apart. Links --link underlined. Code blocks: --type-code 14/24 on a transparent ground with a 2 px --editor-block-rule left rule and a Copy icon button (--tutor-message-copy-button 28 px with a 16 px glyph; hit area --tutor-message-copy-hit: 28 fine / 44 coarse); inline code on --editor-inline-bg; display math bare and centred with overflow scroll. Citations [Page N] are --link in --type-caption with a 44 px hit area on coarse pointers (--tutor-message-citation-hit). The feedback toolbar is a row of 28 px icon buttons (16 px glyphs, 44 px targets on coarse pointers) on one 28 px line; the two thumbs are toggles (aria-pressed) and the chosen one is drawn as a filled glyph in --selection-text, the other as an outline. The panel's chrome (header, session bar, model select) is compact tool chrome on every route, student pages included (36 px icon buttons), while the message region is a comfortable reading surface (16/24); on coarse pointers the chrome's controls carry 44 px hit areas. The composer (the user's decision of 2026-10-19) is one text box with Send and Stop inside it: the box takes --tutor-message-composer-radius (the sheet radius, 8 px), at least --tutor-message-composer-min-height (44 px) and a 1 px --border-interactive edge, which becomes the 2 px --focus-ring frame while its text has focus; at its right end, inside the border, sits one 32 px round icon button (--tutor-message-composer-action; hit area --tutor-message-composer-action-hit, 32 with a fine pointer, 44 with a coarse one, the drawing never grows). Send is an up arrow in the primary style (--accent-solid fill, its 1 px --accent-solid-border edge, the arrow in --accent-on-solid), faded as the disabled primary while the box is empty; while Kiwi answers it becomes Stop, a --text ring around a filled --text square on the surface. The helper line under the box ("Kiwi is answering. Select Stop to interrupt.") stays, and the accessible names stay "Send" and "Stop". While an answer streams the toolbar is hidden until the answer completes. Keyboard: the feedback toolbar is one tab stop with a roving tabindex (Left/Right between its five buttons, Enter or Space presses); citations are links; the Copy button is a tab stop inside its code block; Escape while the composer has focus stops a streaming answer.

pdf-toolbar.$description: The PDF viewer (react-pdf): the toolbar and the surfaces around the paper, on S-02 (file name, previous / next, "n / N", zoom out, "100 %", zoom in, fullscreen), S-09 and A-24 (Search and Thumbnails as tertiary toggles whose pressed look is the tertiary pressed variant (aria-pressed), First, Previous, the page field "3 / 12", Next, Last, zoom, Fit width, Open / print, Fullscreen; the search panel; the thumbnail strip). The bar is tool chrome on both areas: 44 px, on --surface with a 1 px --border-subtle bottom rule, holding compact (36 px) icon buttons with --icon-default glyphs, the file name in --type-label, page and zoom labels in --type-caption tabular --text-secondary, 1 px × 18 px --border-subtle dividers, and the page field as a compact field (--border-interactive). The scroll area is the canvas (--background) with --space-panel padding; each page is paper on a 1 px --paper-frame hairline (no shadow: docked surfaces cast none), dimmed to 92 % in dark mode (--pdf-toolbar-paper-dim → --opacity-paper-dim) so the white paper does not glare; the page the chat has in context carries a 2 px --border-interactive frame on its own edge (one frame, the extra pixel inward) and the bar shows the neutral "In context" chip, so the cue is not colour alone and no brand colour touches the paper's edge (TD-08). Marks drawn on the paper never follow the mode (G5): comment pins visible to students are --on-paper-pin discs with the 16 px speech-bubble glyph in --on-paper-page (the system's own SVG: an emoji ignores color, has no token and varies by platform); hidden-from-students pins (A-24) are --on-paper-page discs with a 2 px --on-paper-pin ring; chunk boxes are 1 px --on-paper-chunk, the selected chunk 2 px --on-paper-pin over the --on-paper-wash, the drag box dashed --on-paper-chunk. The search panel is a floating --surface sheet (1 px --border, --shadow-1) with a compact field, Find (secondary) and Next match (tertiary) and a status line; the thumbnail strip shows paper miniatures on hairline frames on the canvas, the current one outlined like the page, with --type-caption page numbers. The summary banner is an info alert (--status-info-surface, the i glyph and text in --status-info-text, Read as its action, an icon-button close) floating at the top of the viewer with --shadow-1; its re-show button is a neutral icon button with the neutral count badge. The student page's icon rail and "Class Materials" drawer are a panel with sidebar-item rows (the selected file: selection tint + check glyph) and two exclusive filter chips (Lecture / Recitation). Keyboard: the toolbar is one tab stop with a roving tabindex (Left/Right move between its buttons, Enter/Space press; the page field takes digits and Enter); Escape closes the search panel and returns focus to Search.

chart.$description: Phase 6 (2026-10-18), the data colours (kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Chart tokens): five categorical series at one target lightness per mode (± 0.07), the neutral for Other and Unknown, and the chart chrome roles as references. Registered under the reserved namespace and never edited into the three tiers; every token names its CSS property, so the resolver's naming rule is untouched. The series and the neutral are literals derived by derive-chart.mjs from recorded OKLCH parameters (§ 5 admits a chart.* literal that carries `derived`; § 16 re-renders and re-asserts it), replacing the interim palette.chart stand-ins of Phase 3.

derivation.model: Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009) at severity 1.0, in linear sRGB; distances are Euclidean in OKLab × 100
derivation.order: slot 1 is the accent hue; slots 2–5 maximise the minimum adjacent distance (14.78)
derivation.note: At one exact lightness per mode five hue-separated series cannot clear the colour-blind gate at muted chroma (best 6.3 at C <= 0.14; 8.2 only at C 0.22, with a normal-vision minimum of 8.7): lightness is the channel dichromats keep. At ± 0.06 the gate still fails at C <= 0.14 (7.9) and passes at C 0.15 by 0.09 only; ± 0.07 at C <= 0.14 is the smallest band, in steps of 0.01, that clears both gates with a margin (DESIGN.md § Chart tokens › Matched lightness, as measured).
